anti_overlap: Focuses on information hierarchy and progressive disclosure from wayfinding design, not format structure or visual compression
decision_lens: Evaluates whether the information hierarchy matches the decision sequence — show what the navigator needs NOW, defer everything else
distance_rationale: Physical navigation signage and terminal state encoding both solve conveying spatial information for decision-making under attention constraints.
expected_isomorphisms: Progressive disclosure hierarchy, decision-point focus, landmark-based orientation, and information density thresholds all transfer to terminal state encoding.
focus: Wayfinding and signage design — how physical navigation systems convey spatial information through hierarchical progressive disclosure
name: fd-wayfinding-signage-hierarchy
persona: Environmental graphic designer specializing in hospital and airport wayfinding systems, who understands how to guide decision-making through minimal, hierarchically organized visual cues
review_areas: Progressive disclosure hierarchy — wayfinding shows broad direction first, then specific route, then final destination. Terminal state could be disclosed progressively.
Decision-point signage — signs appear at decision points, not continuously. Terminal state updates should focus on where the agent needs to make a choice.
Landmark-based navigation — wayfinding uses landmarks not coordinates. Terminal navigation could use landmarks (prompt, error block, menu).
Information overload thresholds — wayfinding research shows maximum useful sign density before confusion. Maps to: maximum useful terminal state detail before LLM confusion.

severity_examples.condition: Terminal header, content, status bar all encoded at same detail — no hierarchy
severity_examples.scenario: All information at same priority level

severity_examples.condition: Agent must parse entire screen to find where it should look

source_domain: Wayfinding and environmental graphic design (hospital/airport navigation systems)
success_hints: Proposes a hierarchical encoding where the agent can quickly orient (which region matters?) before diving into detail
task_context: Wayfinding research quantifies how much information a navigator can absorb at each decision point. LLM agents navigating terminal UIs face the same cognitive budget.
